rv.q: This intriguing world premiere by playwright Kelsey Mesa frames historical background of the resistance fighters Freddie and Truus Oversteegen from 1940 to 1945 amidst the human drama, fierce loyalty and even the humor and pride---in episodic, almost pulp wartime comic book design style.

Mesa has again dug into a potent political aspect of women’s history and brought forth a stunning, must-see stage event that is as surprisingly and delightfully funny as it is psychologically and ethically profound.

cn.t: Critics praise this WWII resistance drama for its surprising tonal subversion, blending pulpy thrills and unexpected humor with the serious story of Nazi-fighting sisters into a gripping, high-energy theatrical experience.
